notes.decision: Lycopolitan numeral 'four' (= Sahidic ϥⲧⲟⲟⲩ). The Coptic ⲡϩⲧⲁⲩ is the collective form 'the Four.'

ϩⲧⲟⲉ = 'fourth part, watch' (cf. Sah. ϩⲧⲟⲉ). 'The fourth watch of the night' — a temporal frame for the Teacher's discourse. Could also read as 'the four (watches)' but the singular construction with ⲧ- favors 'fourth.'
Greek loanword φωστήρ 'illuminator, luminary.' Standard title of Mani in the Kephalaia. Translated 'the Illuminator.'

From ⲧⲱϩⲙ̄ 'to call, summon, invite' with 3pl object (Lyc. ⲍ = Sah. ϩ). Translated 'they were summoned' / 'they called them' depending on syntactic context. The cognate noun ⲧⲱⲍⲙⲉ ('call/summons') appears at line 17 and 28.
Literally 'the first calls/summonings.' The Twelve Great Rich Gods are identified as the 'first summonings' before the Greatness — i.e., the primal acts of calling forth.
ⲥⲱⲣ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'to scatter, spread out' with 3pl pronoun. The Twelve Gods are deployed three-by-three to the four climes (κλίματα).

Greek στῦλος + ⲉⲁⲩ ('glory') = 'the Pillar of Glory,' technical Manichaean title for the cosmic Atlas figure who bears the refined light upward — also called the Great Omophoros (Ὠμοφόρος, 'shoulder-bearer').
Lycopolitan = Sahidic ϩⲣⲟϣ 'burden, weight.' The Five Sons (of First Man and of Spirit) are those who bear the cosmic burdens.

'Their ten brothers.' This is the key arithmetic of the Twelve Hours of the Third Great Day: 5 sons of First Man + 5 sons of the Spirit = 10, plus the Call (ⲧⲱⲍⲙⲉ) and the Hearing (ⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ) = 12. Not 'their midst' (ⲙⲏⲧⲉ); ⲙⲏⲧ here is the cardinal number 'ten.'
Variant spelling of ⲡⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲉ 'the Radiance,' title of Jesus. Cf. accumulated vocabulary.
ϩⲟⲩ = 'day' (Lycopolitan reflex of Sah. ϩⲟⲟⲩ); plural 'days.' The Twelve Wisdoms are equated with the (twelve) days of light.
Read as ⲛⲁϩⲧⲉ 'faith, trust' (verbal noun from ⲛⲁϩⲧⲉ 'to believe'). 'Every one who shall know them in faith.' The phrase parallels line 5 (ⲉⲧⲛⲁⲥⲟⲩⲱⲛⲟⲩ).

Translated as 'night.' ⲟⲩϣⲛ is the Lycopolitan form of Sahidic ⲟⲩϣⲏ 'night' (feminine, agreeing with feminine ⲧϣⲁⲣⲡ 'first' and ⲧⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲧⲉ 'second'). The chapter establishes a structural parallel: just as there are four DAYS (ⲛⲍⲟⲟⲩⲉ) of light, so there are four NIGHTS (ⲟⲩϣⲛ) of darkness — each Night being a cosmic level of the dark realm. First Night = Land of Darkness; Second = Matter; Third = five worlds of flesh.

Translated 'the image-painter' from Greek ζωγράφος ('painter of living things'). Confirmed by line 12's verbal form ⲧⲉⲧⲁⲥⲍⲱⲣⲡⲁⲫⲉ ('she who painted/depicted'), corresponding to ζωγραφεῖν. Matter is named here as the cosmic image-maker who paints/imprints forms — a striking technical Manichaean designation for hyle as the principle that gives shape to the archontic order.

Translated 'shadows' (= ⲛϩⲁⲓⲃⲉⲥ). The Twelve Shadows of darkness parallel the Twelve Aeons/Rich Gods of light established in earlier kephalaia. ⲍⲁⲃⲉⲥ as Lycopolitan reflex of ϩⲁⲓⲃⲉⲥ 'shadow' fits the cosmological register where each light-being has a corresponding dark shadow.

Translated 'the desire of death' (Greek ἐνθύμησις). Standard Manichaean technical term: matter as the personified concupiscence that desires death. Note: ⲉⲛⲑⲩⲙⲏⲥⲓⲥ is the Greek equivalent of Coptic ⲡⲥⲁⲭⲛⲉ ('counsel') in the five-faculty system, but here used in negative cosmological register for the dark counterpart.

Translated 'she stood firm.' The standard idiom ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'stand fast/firm' with feminine suffix. Matter takes her stand for the war against the divinity — preserving the military-cosmic posture of the Manichaean primal battle.
Translated 'strife' / 'conflict' (= Sah. ⲡⲗⲁϩ from ⲗⲁϩ 'fight, strife'). Forms the standard war-pair with ⲡⲡⲟⲗⲉⲙⲟⲥ 'war' to denote the cosmic primordial battle.
Translated 'the divinity.' Lycopolitan ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲃ = abstract noun from ⲛⲁⲃ/ⲛⲟⲩⲧⲉ 'god' = 'godhood, divinity.' Cf. accumulated vocabulary's ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲟ̄ 'the Greatness' (different abstract from ⲛⲁⲟ 'great').

Translated 'the heat and the cold.' ⲡⲍⲙⲁⲙ = ⲡϩⲙⲟⲙ 'heat'; ⲡⲁⲣⲁϣ = ⲡⲱⲣϣ̄ 'cold.' These are correspondentially identified in line 27 as 'the father and the mother, their fire and their pleasure (hēdonē)' — the cosmic-biological pair generating the lower world.
Translated 'the mother.' ⲧⲙⲟ = ⲧⲙⲁⲩ 'the mother' with Lycopolitan vowel reduction ⲁⲩ → ⲟ. Paired with ⲡⲓⲱⲧ 'the father' as cosmic dyad.

Translated 'which they begot.' ⲭⲡⲁ⸗ⲥ = ϫⲡⲟ-ⲥ 'beget her.' The second Night (Matter) is generated from / emanated from the first Night (Land of Darkness) — establishing the genealogical hierarchy of dark realms.

Translated 'the Living Spirit.' ⲡⲛⲁ = ⲡⲛⲉⲩⲙⲁ; ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ = ⲉⲧⲟⲛϩ 'living.' Standard Manichaean technical title for the Living Spirit (Mihryazd / Spiritus Vivens) who works alongside the First Man in defeating and binding the dark powers.

The character ⳨ in this manuscript appears to function variously: in line 6 (ⲉⲩ⳨ⲣⲉⲛ ⲁⲣⲁⲥ 'they call her') it represents ϯ in the idiom ϯⲣⲉⲛ 'give-name'; in line 18 (ⲛ̄⳨ⲙⲁⲍⲥⲧⲟⲉ 'the seventh') it appears to function as the simple article ⲧ. In line 1 the value of ⲧ⳨ⲉ is unclear — possibly ⲧϯⲉ or a graphic abbreviation. I preserve the character and translate the structure ('the ⳨ⲉ of the women') without forcing a reading.
Read as ⲉⲩϯⲣⲉⲛ ⲁⲣⲁⲥ = 'they give-name to her' = 'they call her' — the standard Coptic idiom ϯⲣⲉⲛ. The staurogram-like ⳨ functions here as ϯ.

From Greek σταυρόω 'to crucify.' Refers to the Living Spirit's cosmological act of binding/fixing the dwelling-place, mapping onto the Manichaean myth of the Spirit's crucifixion of the dark powers in the firmament.

Translated 'seventh' tentatively. The form ⲥⲧⲟⲉ may derive from ⲥⲁϣϥⲉ '7' via Lycopolitan reduction, or alternatively from ϥⲧⲟⲟⲩ '4'. The recurrence in lines 18 and 25 suggests a fixed ordinal designation in this kephalaion's enumeration of dwellings.

ⲕⲱⲕ ⲁⲍⲏⲩ = ⲕⲱⲕ ⲁϩⲏⲩ 'strip naked' (Crum 101a). The twelve doctrines as 'strippings-naked' — i.e. they are the agents that denude the soul of light. Standard Manichaean idiom for the deceptive teachings of error.

From Greek ζῴδιον 'small figure, zodiac sign.' The ⲙⲛⲧⲥⲛⲁⲩⲥ ⲛⲍⲱⲇⲟⲛ = 'twelve zodiac-signs' is the standard Manichaean designation for the twelve cosmic constellations governed by the Zodiac/Sphere of darkness — the visible cosmic frame of matter.

Greek σώφρονες 'the prudent ones' (plural). Used here ironically/inversely of the twelve zodiac-signs as 'sober/prudent' regulators that paint and manifest the cosmos out of the Ancient One. Possible alternative: ἄφρονες 'foolish ones' (negation prefix), but plain σώφρονες fits the ζωγραφέω 'paint/depict' that follows (cosmic painters as ordering rationality of matter).
From Greek ζωγραφέω 'to paint, depict.' The twelve zodiacal signs paint/depict the cosmos as living images. Preserves the Manichaean image of the cosmic frame as a 'painting' projected from matter.

Translated 'the Ancient One.' Likely ⲣⲙ̄-ⲛ̄-ⲏⲥⲉ 'person of old/antiquity' (cf. Sah. ⲏⲥ 'old'). Functions as a cosmic title for the figure who reigns in the doctrines and from whom the twelve zodiac-signs emanate. Capitalized as a hypostatized cosmic principle. Alternative reading 'the prudent/wise one' (ⲣⲙ̄ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ) is possible but less morphologically natural.
ⲇⲁⲕⲣⲓⲛⲉ likely from Greek δια-κρίνειν 'discriminate, judge'; ⲙⲫⲟⲟⲩ = ⲙ̄ⲡⲟⲟⲩ 'today.' Translated 'judges them today.' Possible alternative: ⲙⲫⲟⲟⲩ as object pronoun, less likely.
From ⲟⲩⲱⲗⲡ̄ 'uncover, reveal, lay bare.' Translated 'were uncovered/revealed' — preserves the unveiling sense of the Manichaean cosmological revelation of darkness.

Translated 'were separated' tentatively, taking the verb as variant of ⲟⲩⲱⲧⲃ̄ 'transfer, change' or related to ⲟⲩⲱⲧ 'be different.' The reciprocal ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲛ̄ⲛⲟⲩⲉⲣⲏⲩ 'from one another' supports a separation/distinguishing sense.

Greek ὑπάρχοντα 'things existing, possessions, substances.' Preserved as Greek term to flag its philosophical-technical sense — the things-existing as substantial beings revealed at the eschatological unveiling.
